slides.subtitle: The six links that must connect for an infectious disease to spread — break any link to stop transmission.

slides.heading: Contact Transmission
bullets: Horizontal — immediate transfer person to person.
Vertical — mother to child in utero (placenta) or during childbirth.
Indirect contact — via a non-living object (fomite = vehicle transmission).
Vector-borne — a living organism carries the pathogen to another.

slides.heading: Other Modes & Portal of Entry
bullets: Enteric — feces of an infected person to the mouth of another.
Portals of entry: mouth, nose, eyes, rashes, cuts, needlestick injuries, surgical wounds, IV sites.
Protect entry: wound/IV dressings, remove tubes early, masks/goggles, prevent needlesticks, food & water safety.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Six links: agent → reservoir → exit → transmission → entry → susceptible host.
Droplet (PIMP) = within 1 m, >5 microns; Airborne (MTV) = any distance, <5 microns.
Bacteria = most common agent; viruses = most microscopic.
Break ANY link (e.g., hand hygiene) to stop the spread.
